title: EventPrune: Cascaded Event-Assisted Token Pruning for Efficient Embodied Spatial Reasoning
claim: Prior pruning discards the structure needed for spatial queries; ours keeps it and stays above full-token accuracy at high sparsity.
layout: 3 panels: top task input, bottom-left masked-frame contrast, bottom-right line plot
description: The figure has three dashed-border panels. The top panel shows two indoor video frames on a time arrow, labeled Video Input, next to a beige speech bubble that asks for the distance between the sofa and the TV, labeled Spatial Tasks. The bottom-left panel has two rows of darkened frames where only a few patches stay visible. The Other Method row keeps scattered patches, circled in white, and is labeled Lack Physical Structure. The OURS row keeps contiguous patches around the sofa, TV and chair, circled in green, and is labeled Rich Physical Structure. Dashed lines link the circled regions. The bottom-right panel is a line chart of relative accuracy against token retention at 20, 50 and 70 percent. A bold green Ours (ECP) line sits above the dashed full-token baseline and the other pruning methods. A +9% arrow marks the gap at 20 percent.
caption: Token pruning for spatial reasoning. Unlike prior pruning, ECP preserves task-relevant geometric cues under high sparsity.
abstract: Embodied spatial reasoning requires models to track continuous motion and precise geometric structure, but the quadratic attention cost of Transformer-based Video-LLMs makes dense visual tokens computationally expensive. Existing token pruning paradigms predominantly rely on discrete static snapshots, failing to preserve the motion and geometric cues essential for reasoning. We propose Event Cascade Pruning (ECP), to our knowledge the first training-free framework that leverages the high-frequency motion cues from event cameras as a continuous event-guided motion prior to guide token selection. ECP combines three stages: Event-Guided Temporal Sampling to anchor motion-informative keyframes, Event-guided Motion Saliency Filtering to suppress event-inactive visual tokens, and Event-Attention Ranking Fusion to calibrate spatial attention with motion-salient dynamics. With 80\% visual token reduction, ECP outperforms the full-token baseline (37.62\% vs.\ 36.31\%) while achieving 1.89$\times$ inference speedup and 52\% GFLOPs reduction. We further introduce ESR-Real, the first real-world RGB-event benchmark for embodied spatial reasoning, where ECP improves accuracy by 2.68 percentage points over full-token baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/Ma-Potter/EventPrune.
